┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORKS — RELATIONSHIP MAP                │
│                                                                          │
│  SCOPE: applies to ALL traditions                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│  │  CAMPBELL (1949) — Monomyth / Hero's Journey                    │    │
│  │  Pattern: universal hero arc (departure → initiation → return)  │    │
│  │  Mechanism: psychological — individuation, transformation       │    │
│  │  Critique: over-fits; forces non-heroic myths into hero frame   │    │
│  │                                                                 │    │
│  │  JUNG (1875–1961) — Archetypes / Collective Unconscious         │    │
│  │  Pattern: recurring symbols (shadow, anima, self, trickster)   │    │
│  │  Mechanism: psychological — shared deep cognitive structures    │    │
│  │  Relation: Campbell operationalizes Jung's archetypes           │    │
│  │           (Campbell = Journey; Jung = symbol inventory)         │    │
│  │                                                                 │    │
│  │  LÉVI-STRAUSS (1955) — Structural Analysis                      │    │
│  │  Pattern: binary oppositions (nature/culture, life/death)       │    │
│  │  Mechanism: cognitive — myths as logical operators on paradox   │    │
│  │  Competes with Campbell/Jung: not psychology but logic;         │    │
│  │  the narrative content is irrelevant, only structure matters   │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                          │
│  SCOPE: explains specific cross-cultural pattern                         │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  FRAZER (1890) — Comparative Religion / Golden Bough            │    │
│  │  Pattern: dying-and-rising god; sacred king; vegetation cycle   │    │
│  │  Mechanism: ecological — seasonal agricultural ritual as base   │    │
│  │  Status: influential but contested; over-reduces differences    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                          │
│  SCOPE: Indo-European traditions ONLY (not applicable to non-IE)         │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  DUMÉZIL (1958) — Indo-European Trifunctionalism                │    │
│  │  Pattern: sovereignty / warrior / productive — in every IE      │    │
│  │  pantheon (Vedic, Roman, Norse, Celtic, Iranian, Baltic)        │    │
│  │  Mechanism: historical — inherited from Proto-Indo-European     │    │
│  │  Complements Lévi-Strauss: structural, not psychological;       │    │
│  │  historically reconstructable, not universal-cognitive          │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                          │
│  COMPETITION AXIS: Psychology (Campbell/Jung) ←→ Anthropology (Dumézil) │
│                    Universal cognition (LS) ←→ Historical transmission   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    THE HERO'S JOURNEY                            │
│                                                                  │
│           DEPARTURE              INITIATION           RETURN     │
│                                                                  │
│  Ordinary ──→ Call to ──→ Refusal ──→ Crossing ──→ Road of       │
│  World       Adventure   of Call      Threshold    Trials        │
│                                                                  │
│                                    ──→ Supreme ──→ Ordeal        │
│                                        Road of      Abyss        │
│                                        Trials                    │
│                                                                  │
│                                    ──→ Reward ──→ Road Back      │
│                                                                  │
│  ←── Return with ←── Resurrection ←── Crossing ←── Elixir/       │
│       Elixir                          Return        Boon         │
│                                       Threshold                  │
│                                                                  │
│  Examples:                                                       │
│  Odysseus: Ithaca → Trojan War → Return (20 years)               │
│  Gilgamesh: Uruk → Cedar Forest → Underworld → Uruk              │
│  Arjuna: Battlefield → Bhagavad Gita revelation → Battle         │
│  Luke Skywalker: Tatooine → Death Star → Endor (consciously      │
│  modeled on Campbell by George Lucas)                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

CREATION FROM NOTHING (ex nihilo):
  Egyptian: sun-god Atum speaks/thinks world into being
  Abrahamic: God speaks ("Let there be light")
  Maori: Te Kore (void) → Te Po (darkness) → Te Ao (light)

CREATION FROM CHAOS / PRIMORDIAL WATERS:
  Mesopotamian: Tiamat (salt water) + Apsu (fresh water) → world
  Greek: Chaos → Gaia → Ouranos
  Hindu: cosmic ocean, Vishnu sleeping on Ananta serpent

WORLD PARENT:
  Maori: Ranginui (sky father) + Papatuanuku (earth mother),
         separated by children to let light in
  Greek: Ouranos (sky) + Gaia (earth) — similar separation

EARTH DIVER:
  Native American (Iroquois, Ojibwe): animal dives into primal waters,
  brings up mud from which earth is formed
  Siberian: loon/duck dives → world formed from mud

WORLD EGG:
  Hindu: cosmic egg (Brahmanda) splits into heaven and earth
  Finnish (Kalevala): cosmic egg laid by bird on Väinämöinen's knee
  Orphic Greek: Phanes hatches from silver egg

DISMEMBERMENT OF PRIMORDIAL BEING:
  Norse: Ymir's body → world (flesh→earth, blood→sea, skull→sky)
  Hindu: Purusha → universe in Rigveda
  Mesopotamian: Tiamat's body → sky and earth

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                TRICKSTER FIGURES ACROSS CULTURES                 │
├─────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Loki (Norse)    │ Shape-shifter, chaos agent, Ragnarok instigator│
│ Hermes (Greek)  │ Messenger, thief, psychopomp, inventor of lyre │
│ Coyote (N. Am.) │ Transformer, culture hero, foolish and wise    │
│ Raven (N. Am.)  │ Creator-trickster; brings light/fire to humans │
│ Anansi (Akan)   │ Spider, wisdom keeper, ancestor of all stories │
│ Eshu (Yoruba)   │ Crossroads trickster, oracular interpreter     │
│ Sun Wukong      │ Monkey King, disrupts cosmic order, redeemed   │
│ Maui (Polynesia)│ Culture hero, snares sun, fishes up islands    │
│ Coyote/Br. Rabbit│ Weaker defeats stronger through wit           │
└─────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Trickster function: disrupts order, tests limits, enables creativity,
often creates culture (fire, language, tools) through transgression

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              INDO-EUROPEAN MYTHOLOGICAL CORRESPONDENCES          │
│                                                                  │
│  THEME          GREEK      ROMAN      VEDIC       NORSE          │
│  ─────────────  ─────────  ─────────  ──────────  ────────────   │
│  Sky Father     Zeus       Jupiter    Dyaus Pita  Tyr/Tiw        │
│  (PIE: *Dyēus)  (Dis Pater)(Deus)     (Deiwo)     (Tiwaz)        │
│  Thunder God    Zeus       Jupiter    Indra       Thor           │
│  Sea/Fate       Poseidon   Neptune    Varuna      Njord/Odin     │
│  Blacksmith     Hephaestus Vulcan     Tvashtri    —              │
│  Dawn goddess   Eos        Aurora     Ushas       Ēostre         │
│  Twins          Dioscuri   Gemini     Ashvins     Alcis          │
│  Dragon battle  Apollo    —          Indra/Vrtra Thor/Jörmungandr│

blocks.heading_context: ## Myth and History: Sources and Transmission
blocks.text:
PRIMARY SOURCES by tradition:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ GREEK:       Homer (Iliad/Odyssey ~800BCE), Hesiod           │
│              (Theogony/Works+Days), Homeric Hymns,           │
│              Aeschylus/Sophocles/Euripides, Ovid (Roman)     │
│ NORSE:       Prose Edda (Snorri Sturluson ~1220 CE)          │
│              Poetic Edda (collected ~1270 CE)                │
│              Both written by Christians 200+ yrs after       │
│              Christianization — bias present                 │
│ MESOPOTAMIAN:Enuma Elish (7 tablets, ~1100 BCE)              │
│              Epic of Gilgamesh (Standard Version ~1300 BCE)  │
│ HINDU:       Rigveda (~1500 BCE), Mahabharata (~400 BCE),    │
│              Ramayana (~300 BCE), Puranas (300–1200 CE)      │
│ EGYPTIAN:    Pyramid Texts (2400 BCE), Coffin Texts,         │
│              Book of the Dead (~1550 BCE), temple carvings   │
│ CELTIC:      NO pre-Christian primary sources!               │
│              Irish manuscripts 7th–12th CE (Christian monks) │
│              Welsh: Mabinogion 11th–13th CE manuscripts      │
│ MESOAMERICAN:Popol Vuh (Kiche Maya, ~1554 CE, post-Conquest) │
│              Colonial-period Aztec codices                   │
│ SLAVIC:      NO primary mythological texts survived          │
│              Reconstructed from folklore, chronicles,        │
│              archaeology, and comparative IE evidence        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
